1.explanation: All of the C++ syntax rules live in the default export function of cpp.js: this function defines how templates, operators, expression contexts and declarations are tokenized. Because the grammar in cpp.js does not properly recognize “<<” in this context (nor does it correctly parse the template argument list “<<1,2,3,4,5;”), the highlighter falls back to plain text. Fixing the bug requires updating cpp.js’s language modes (inside the default export) to include operator<< as a valid stream-insertion operator and to correctly handle nested angle-bracket templates in expressions.
1.bug_scenario: When running hljs.highlight on C++ code that uses Eigen’s template types and the stream‐insertion operator “<<” (e.g. vector<<1,2,3,4,5; and printing with std::cout << C), the highlighter fails to parse and style those lines correctly. In the screenshots you can see that the “<<” operator and the template argument lists are left un-highlighted or break the surrounding syntax.

2.explanation: All of the C++ highlighting rules are defined inside the anonymous default export in cpp.js.  That function builds the grammar for comments, numbers, strings, preprocessor directives, expression contexts and template-angle parsing.  The failure to handle back-to-back “< <” (as in vector<<…) and re-enter an expression-or-initializer context lives in that exported function’s rule definitions (template-argument regex, expression context variants, and operator handling).  Editing the grammar inside export default function(hljs) is therefore where the fix must be made.
